q: Everyone keeps telling me to swim but I find that I get to the pool and have zero idea what to do and what would be the most effective for pain relief/exercise and everything I find online is so overwhelming.
cx: At 21 weeks with back and rib pain, she wants a concrete routine, not general advice.

q: I am paying for a prenatal workout series and she puts such an emphasis on posterior chain. I just do not do them enough. I think I am literally scaring myself out of so many things due to how bad the pain can get.
cx: Same woman on a paid prenatal workout programme she rarely does, out of fear of pain.

q: I want to feel strong the last half of my pregnancy and I do not feel that way at all right now due to all of this.
cx: Same woman on what she wants from the second half.

q: I’m so ready to have this baby and meet my baby but I can’t shake this dreadful feeling, like I don’t know I feel so numb idk if it’s because my mom is in jail so I will have my first baby by myself with just me and my bf or what.
cx: At 38+4, a scheduled section for a big baby in days, with no family support.

q: a few weeks ago, I spent an entire Saturday sobbing and gagging between washing the dishes, taking breaks, throwing up, going back to washing more dishes. It was a miserable day.
cx: At 14 weeks, living with unhelpful roommates, smells make the dishes impossible.

q: I bought my roommate a chipotle gift card in exchange for his help cleaning the dishes I was having a crisis over. Disposables have since become my best friends
cx: Same woman a week later on what fixed it.

q: I said it several times to my midwife and she very reluctantly referred me to a physiotherapist, and then nothing. When I asked her about it she told me that the referral was refused.
cx: UK mother, five months postpartum, still in pelvic pain since month four of pregnancy.

q: I'd like to go private but being on maternity leave I'm tight on money, but if I know the NHS won't do anything for me then we can make the little financial effort to fit that in
cx: Same mother weighing private physiotherapy against waiting on NHS referrals.

q: We never got a HV, and I never bothered to call to ask for one as I've been told by other mums that they're useless.
cx: Same mother on the health visitor she never saw.

q: My husband, my mom & my in-laws are amazing with him & he is very well cared for. Everything I try to do for the baby, everyone else just does it so so much better.
cx: Three weeks after a hard birth, a mother feels the family has taken over the baby.

q: My husband and my mom were very scared about my health and were paranoid about me getting enough sleep so they just took over the baby most of the time.
cx: Same mother on how help in the first weeks left her out.

q: Yes there is a registry, yes we know what we need, yes I am scared of birthing a child, no your unsolicited advice is not helpful, yes we want to know the sex
cx: A pregnant woman's list of answers to the questions everyone asks her.

q: yes we are looking at car seats and strollers, yes I am planning to breastfeed, yes I am planning on having a vaginal birth, yes I will use drugs if I need them, no I do not want to give birth in a bathtub, yes I have done research into every topic you can think of to bring up
cx: Same list: her birth and buying plans, answered for the hundredth time.

q: yes I have a plan to go on maternity leave, no we haven't fully mapped out what that will look like, yes we have a community
cx: Same list: leave and support.

q: Anything you purchased that you wish you’d had sooner? I’m pretty much done on the nesting front and am fully prepped for her to arrive
cx: UK first-timer at 32 weeks, fully prepared, asks how to make the last weeks easier.

q: We only prepped so early because I’m insane honestly 😂
cx: Same woman on preparing early.

q: My company is really stingy with mat leave but lets you roll over all your annual leave, so I’m storing it up to use the other side instead — so will be working right up to 40 weeks 🙈🙈 dreading it tbh
cx: Same woman on working to her due date to save leave for after.

q: I even bought a toothpaste with no scent/flavour, thinking that would help, but somehow it still makes me feel disgusted.
cx: Brushing teeth makes her vomit daily.

q: My normally sweet angel child has turned into a rage monster overnight, I am so tired, my body hurts, and today for the first time since my son was a newborn I cried while holding him.
cx: At 36 weeks with a two-year-old who has suddenly started fighting bedtime.

q: he has started pushing the boundaries a lot with getting out of bed at night (we had to switch to a toddler bed a couple weeks ago). We’ve been up since 5am and I barely slept
cx: Same mother, alone with the toddler for two nights.

q: We had our immediate family come to the hospital, and to be honest it was a lot. I couldn't even get out of bed. Looking back, I regret the decision as I felt it put me behind on sleep I desperately needed before entering the newborn trenches.
cx: A first-time mother one week after a birth with an unexpected cut, on hospital visitors.

q: it is impossible to ignore the pressure from family members to visit, or for us to visit them. Of course they are excited, but the idea of having people over when I can barely walk some days has been emotionally exhausting. I have tried to explain that im recovering from labor, but I feel people are quick to brush it off.
cx: Same mother, home a few days.

q: I just ate a slice of frozen pizza that was over a year expired (even though I just bought it last month from the store 🙃). [...] Now I’m freaking out. I’m in the first trimester. How eff’d are me and my baby?
cx: First trimester, panicking after eating something expired.

q: The thought of it makes me feel claustrophobic… like I’m being tickled from the inside but the tickler refuses to let up. Basically it’s the fear of loss of control over my body.
cx: At 14 weeks, afraid of feeling the baby move.

q: I’m learning to embrace it let’s put it that way lol I’m just glad to know she’s okay in there. None of it ended up being as weird as I feared.
cx: Same woman three weeks later, now feeling movement.

q: Baby is cluster feeding and I’m being told my milk must not be rich enough, baby is not eating enough per feed, there is something wrong.
cx: Ten days after a section, in-laws who help also give constant feeding advice.

q: it’s become non stop advice especially from SIL who has no children and gets all her info from Tik tok vids she keeps sending (I don’t have time right now to watch them all).
cx: Same mother on a sister-in-law's TikTok advice.

q: Today they started dusting my house (I cleaned it before hospital), scrubbing my new baby bathtub before first use (overkill), and rearranging my living room because it’s “cluttered”.
cx: Same mother on in-laws taking over her home.

q: my mom stayed over for the first week home to help out. She’s always lived with her MIL so she’s good about not giving unsolicited advice and was a great help.
cx: Same mother: her own mother's first-week stay worked.

q: Hubbie said they’re just trying to help and I get that but it’s. Too. Much.
cx: Same mother on her husband's response.
